comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
the same as any other project, IMHO 

Credit everyone involved. If you use assets or code from someone, that goes in the credits. If you found a particular source really useful, that should also go in the credits under a thank-you section. 

The model and the people who made it should 100% go in your credits. Without their work, your project would not exist. 

  
Whatever you fckn do, DO NOT have a chest-thumping credit section where you just say '\*I\* made this! ME! JUST ME!' 

If you genuinely feel you did 100% of the work and nobody else deserves credit... well, honestly, you're not going to listen to this anyway, but in that case just don't even include a credits page.

comments.author: ThreeDMK
comments.body:
All  my projects include a credits section. 

First is always my brother in law who subsidizes a portion of my AI budget and has since week 1 many months ago.  Dude is a legend.

AI services used and their roles:  Claude for Tools development, Research and Orchestration, OpenAI for bot and gameplay testing, if I used others for anything I would include them here as well, but only if they relate to tools or assets used in the development.

3rd party license agreements for open source free use code I included in my tools.  Mainly for art and audio plugins, but sometimes others.

Paid libraries and services used.

Anyone who assisted in development and testing of the product.

At the end of the day I don’t really care if people dislike AI usage in my projects.  I have nothing to hide.  2 years from now this will be the norm.  People will likely be judged for using weaker models when the top tier models help produce better content.

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body: Yes, have credits, even short ones. Put your name (or studio), then any people who helped or playtested, then a "Tools and assets" section: engine, fonts, music and sound sources with their licenses, and the AI tools you used. You don't need to credit the AI like a person, but listing it as a tool is honest and saves you questions later. Check each asset's license too, since many CC-BY packs require attribution in exactly this spot.
